candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite unlike fractions as equivalent fractions before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts use essentially identical names and definitions for converting unlike fractions to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number, mixed number, or fraction into a subtraction-ready equivalent form without changing its value, such as adding a zero fractional part, standardizing a mixed number, or simplifying a fraction part before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and B are identical; C's 'Normalize fractional form' covers the same preparatory rewriting operations, including whole-plus-zero-fraction, standard mixed-number form, and pre-subtraction simplification.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator by subtracting the numerators and keeping the denominator, including fractional parts of mixed numbers once aligned.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C states the fractional subtraction operation explicitly, while A and B include this within the broader 'Subtract aligned parts'; the overlapping fraction-subtraction component aligns directly here.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers or whole numbers once the operands are in subtraction-ready form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Only expert C separates whole-part subtraction into its own skill. In A and B, whole-part subtraction is bundled together with fraction subtraction inside 'Subtract aligned parts,' so no exact standalone counterpart exists.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same regrouping/borrowing action from the whole-number part into fractional units; wording differs slightly but the cognitive operation is the same.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms or recognize when a fractional result simplifies to a whole number or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and B isolate final reduction as its own skill. C includes this same idea inside a broader combined end-stage skill rather than as a standalone concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine computed whole and fractional parts and present the answer in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and B isolate recombination/final formatting, while C's 'Simplify and combine' includes this same final-form composition along with simplification. The shared concept of expressing the final answer in proper form is present in all three.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks are highly aligned overall. A and B are identical. C matches most concepts but differs in granularity: it splits A/B's 'Subtract aligned parts' into separate fraction and whole-part subtraction skills, and it combines A/B's 'Simplify result' and 'Compose final form' into one broader end-stage skill. All skill IDs from each expert were mapped exactly once, with most concepts showing strong 3/3 consensus and one C-only standalone concept for subtracting whole parts.
